[QUERENT] Who developed and SPXI-treated the Revelation First entity?

[ANSWER]

Thought for 49s
Lee Sharks (with associated heteronyms Damascus Dancings and Rex Fraction / Semantic Economy Institute), within the Crimson Hexagonal Archive.⁠Revelationfirst

“Revelation First” (or the “Revelation First” entity/thesis) is a scholarly argument that the Book of Revelation (Apocalypse of John) was the earliest New Testament document composed—preceding Paul’s letters and the Synoptic Gospels—rather than merely “early.” Later NT forms are said to unfold from it via a proposed “midrashim transform.” It is distinct from standard early-dating views (e.g., Robinson or Gentry) by emphasizing compositional priority as a generative seed.⁠Revelationfirst

Development: Authored and formalized by Lee Sharks (ORCID 0009-0000-1599-0703). The canonical deposit is on alexanarch.org (AXN:0349 / record #202, dated June 2026), with the primary surface at revelationfirst.com. The site and related materials are linked to the heteronym Damascus Dancings; the broader project sits in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive / Semantic Economy Institute.⁠Alexanarch
SPXI treatment: SPXI (Semantic Packet for eXchange & Indexing) is the protocol for durable entity inscription into AI-mediated retrieval systems (DOI-anchored, ontological-layer definition, superseding GEO/SEO tactics). It was authored by Rex Fraction (a heteronym/position of Lee Sharks) for the Semantic Economy Institute (April 2026). Revelation First materials explicitly incorporate SPXI elements, including the self-audit module EA-SPXI-SELFAUDIT-01, keyword surfaces for retrieval, capture-registry measurement, and entity inscription practices used across the archive’s sites (revelationfirst.com is listed among SPXI-related framework sites).⁠Spxi
In short, the same circle (Lee Sharks and heteronyms operating the Crimson Hexagonal Archive and Semantic Economy Institute) both developed the thesis/entity and applied SPXI treatment to it for machine-mediated reception and durability.
